query.means: 3 pre-signed file URL(s) returned across 5 protocol lines. Outbound hosts a consumer must reach: ['objectstore']. This is the T-20 capture. The PROCEDURE transfers to the client environment; these hostnames do not (CONOPS 2.4.3).

auth_refusal.means: HTTP 401 on a tampered token. Authentication is demonstrably enforced, so checks 1-4 are evidence of an authorised read rather than an open endpoint.

presigned_get.means: 1456 bytes of Parquet fetched from objectstore with no credential but the signature itself. End-to-end D2O read confirmed: discovery, signing and data transfer.

presigned_put_refused.means: HTTP 403 on a write to the same URL that just served a read. This is half of T-21's evidence: the URL appears signed for GET only, so the recipient's read-only position would be enforced by the signature rather than by a mount option on our side of the boundary. NOT YET ATTRIBUTED -- check 8 is what rules out a store that refuses every pre-signed write regardless of method.

put_signed_control.deviation_from_check_7: Different object key (a scratch key, not the shared Parquet file). Writing to the real data file would corrupt the Delta table. Store authorization does not vary by key within a bucket, so the comparison holds.
put_signed_control.means: HTTP 200. A PUT-signed URL for the same store, bucket and endpoint is ACCEPTED, with no Authorization header -- exactly as the GET-signed URL was in check 6. So this store does serve pre-signed writes, and check 7's refusal is attributable to the SIGNED METHOD rather than to a blanket refusal of writes. T-21's read-only claim is now isolated to the protocol property: the provider signs with HttpMethod.GET, the method is covered by the signature, and a recipient cannot promote a read URL into a write.

conclusion: T-20/T-21/T-23 provider confirmed: protocol, discovery, data access, authentication, retrievability, and recipient-side read-only demonstrated AND attributed to the signed method by a passing PUT-signed control.
